hook: A passive optical filter gives dim-light microscopy fivefold more information on fine detail
hook_turn: fivefold more information on fine detail
summary: Fourier domain division splits the light in the Fourier plane into regions detected separately, which lowers the photons needed to see fine detail. In a microscopy demonstration, it gave a fivefold gain in Fisher information at high spatial frequencies compared with direct imaging. The gain applies to the photon-starved regime and to specific frequency components, not to all imaging conditions.
title: Passive imaging with quantum advantage.
